objects.description: Lightweight string-info descriptor used across the API to report a buffer’s data pointer, length, and writable capacity. Frequently returned by helper functions (not owning the memory).
Connection protocol callback table instance attached per-connection. User allocates one per connection and sets callbacks to handle socket events and lifecycle.
Parsed URL view holding slices (non-owning) into an original URL buffer for each component.
Argument bundle for fio_write2/fio_write2_fn specifying a buffer or file descriptor to send, deallocation/close callbacks, size, offset, and flags.
Named-argument struct for starting a listening service; contains callbacks and bind parameters.
Named-argument struct used by fio_connect to initiate a non-blocking client connection.
Configuration for fio_start; sets desired number of threads and worker processes with special negative/zero semantics.
Pluggable read/write hooks replacing system I/O for a connection. Implement read, write, optional flush, close handshake and cleanup. Must not call facil I/O APIs inside hooks to avoid deadlocks.
Named-argument bundle for scheduling a protected per-connection task with a specified lock level and fallback on failure/closure.

objects.definition: typedef struct subscription_s subscription_s;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a pub/sub subscription. Actual structure is hidden; used for unsubscribe and inspecting channel.
Engine interface for bridging facil.io pub/sub with external systems. Provides subscribe/unsubscribe/publish callbacks. Instances can be attached/detached.
Message structure delivered to pub/sub subscribers. Contains a numeric filter, channel, message payload, two user data pointers, and a JSON flag. Channel/msg point to immutable buffers.
Named-argument struct for creating a subscription by filter or channel, optional glob-like matcher, callbacks, and user data.
Arguments for publishing a message, including engine selection, target channel, payload, and JSON flag.
Metadata attachment container for pub/sub messages. Extensions return one to stash preprocessed data and a cleanup callback.

objects.definition: typedef uint8_t volatile fio_lock_i;
objects.description: Byte-sized spinlock primitive used with inline helpers fio_trylock/fio_unlock/fio_lock. Initial value FIO_LOCK_INIT (0).
State container for incremental SHA-1 hashing. Initialize with fio_sha1_init, feed with fio_sha1_write, finalize with fio_sha1_result.
State container for incremental SHA-2 hashing supporting multiple variants. Use fio_sha2_init with a variant, then fio_sha2_write and fio_sha2_result.

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
  FIO_CALL_ON_INITIALIZE,
  FIO_CALL_PRE_START,
  FIO_CALL_BEFORE_FORK,
  FIO_CALL_AFTER_FORK,
  FIO_CALL_IN_CHILD,
  FIO_CALL_IN_MASTER,
  FIO_CALL_ON_START,
  FIO_CALL_ON_IDLE,
  FIO_CALL_ON_SHUTDOWN,
  FIO_CALL_ON_FINISH,
  FIO_CALL_ON_PARENT_CRUSH,
  FIO_CALL_ON_CHILD_CRUSH,
  FIO_CALL_AT_EXIT,
  FIO_CALL_NEVER
} callback_type_e;
objects.description: Enumeration for library lifecycle callback types used with fio_state_callback_* APIs.
Enumeration selecting SHA-2 variant for fio_sha2_s hashing state.
Lock levels used to guard access to a connection’s protocol object for scheduled tasks or external access.
Enumeration of synthetic I/O events that can be forced via fio_force_event.
Function type for message metadata providers; invoked before publish to attach preprocessed metadata to pub/sub messages.

objects.definition: typedef int (*fio_match_fn)(fio_str_info_s pattern, fio_str_info_s channel);
objects.description: Channel matching function signature used for patterned subscriptions (e.g., glob). Return 0 unless a match is found.

objects.definition:
typedef enum __attribute__((packed)) {
  FIOBJ_T_NUMBER = 0x01,
  FIOBJ_T_NULL = 0x06,
  FIOBJ_T_TRUE = 0x16,
  FIOBJ_T_FALSE = 0x26,
  FIOBJ_T_FLOAT,
  FIOBJ_T_STRING,
  FIOBJ_T_ARRAY,
  FIOBJ_T_HASH,
  FIOBJ_T_DATA,
  FIOBJ_T_UNKNOWN
} fiobj_type_enum;
objects.description: Packed enumeration of the dynamic FIOBJ object types used for runtime type tagging and dispatch.

objects.definition: typedef uintptr_t FIOBJ;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a facil.io dynamic object, encoded in a uintptr_t. Low bits encode immediate primitives; allocated objects point to headers/vtables.
Lightweight descriptor for a C string/buffer, carrying capacity (if writable), length, and data pointer. Used for returning NUL-terminated or binary-safe strings.
Vtable for FIOBJ dynamic types, providing type name, deallocation, size/count, truthiness, equality, iteration, and conversion to string/integer/float.
Common header stored at the beginning of allocated FIOBJ objects, holding the runtime type tag and atomic reference count.

No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. It only includes other headers and defines a function fiobj_test. Therefore, there are no types to document from this file itself.

Opaque object handle type used throughout the fiobj API to represent objects (here specifically strings). This header only references FIOBJ; it is not defined here. Details about lifetime and representation are unknown from this file. Use fiobj_free to release objects when done, per function comments.
Struct conveying raw C-string view (data pointer and length) of an FIOBJ. Used here via fiobj_obj2cstr to implement fiobj_str_copy. Not defined in this header.

Opaque handle type used by the fiobj dynamic type system, representing any dynamic object (including arrays). It is referenced throughout this header but defined elsewhere (in fiobject.h). Details such as layout and lifetime rules are unknown from this header. Use fiobj_free/fiobj_dup per the API’s documentation.

Opaque handle type for facil.io objects, used here as the hash object and as keys/values. It is referenced but not defined within this header; its real definition is in included headers (fiobject.h). Details such as representation, lifetime rules, and ownership are external to this file.
Built-in typedef used by API; not defined here. Included to note that the header references size_t for capacities and counts, but no new type is defined.
Standard fixed-width unsigned integer type used for hashed key lookup; not defined here.

Opaque handle type for facil.io dynamic objects, used here to represent a Data Stream object (in-memory buffer, temp file, or file descriptor). The actual definition is not present in this header; it is included via <fiobject.h>. Details about lifecycle, allocation, and destruction are unknown from this header alone.

Structure describing a temporary string/buffer view returned by read operations (not NUL-terminated). The concrete struct definition is not in this header; it is referenced from <fiobject.h>. Instances are ephemeral and invalidated by the next operation on the same Data Stream object, as documented by the read functions.

Opaque handle type for fiobj objects (numbers, floats, etc.). This header references FIOBJ in function signatures but does not define it; it is defined in fiobject.h. Details such as lifetime and ownership are managed by the fiobj API (e.g., fiobj_free). Information missing: concrete definition and semantics are not present in this file.

String info structure used by the library to return temporary, thread-safe C string objects. This header only references the type in function declarations and deprecation attributes; the actual structure is defined elsewhere (likely fiobject.h or another header). Information missing: fields, ownership rules, and lifetime guarantees beyond notes in comments.

Opaque mustache template/instruction array handle used by this API. The concrete definition is not present in this header; it is declared in mustache_parser.h. Treat it as an opaque type whose lifetime is managed by fiobj_mustache_free after creation by fiobj_mustache_load or fiobj_mustache_new.

Opaque handle type for FIOBJ objects (Facil.io dynamic objects). Not defined here; declared in fiobject.h. Used as the string/value container for rendering output and providing input data. Lifetime management is outside the scope of this header.
String info/descriptor struct used to pass filename data. Not defined here; declared in fiobject.h. Used only as an argument carrier; ownership remains with the caller.

Aggregate of named arguments for loading/creating a mustache template, including filename/data pointers, lengths, and optional error container. Not defined here; declared in mustache_parser.h. Used by fiobj_mustache_new via designated initializers.

Opaque handle type representing a fiobj object used throughout the fiobj JSON API. This header only references FIOBJ (declared in included headers) and does not define it here; therefore details about its structure and lifecycle are not present in this file.
No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. The file declares SipHash functions and a macro but introduces no new data types.

No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only defines a static inline function fio_tmpfile that creates a temporary file using mkstemp and returns its file descriptor (int). Since the task requires documenting only custom data types, there are none to report.

Pointer-to-pointer to const char used for the NULL-terminated array of option specification strings passed to fio_cli_start (function form). This is not a new type definition but is included here as the only pointer type directly defined in the function signature that represents an owned collection. Note: No custom structs/enums/typedefs/classes are defined in this header.

objects.definition: typedef struct fio_tls_s fio_tls_s;
objects.description: Opaque SSL/TLS context and settings handle for facil.io. Instances are created with fio_tls_new and can have certificates, trust anchors, and ALPN protocols configured. Lifetime is reference-counted: increment with fio_tls_dup and release with fio_tls_destroy. Concrete structure contents are intentionally hidden in this header.
HTTP connection settings for server/client, including callbacks, resource limits, TLS pointer, and websocket options. Required by http_listen/http_connect.
Ephemeral HTTP request/response handle used within callbacks/tasks. Holds method/path/headers/body and response state. Becomes invalid after sending/finish/pause/upgrade.
Enum for the SameSite attribute of cookies.
Named-argument struct for setting an HTTP cookie via http_set_cookie, including value, scope, flags, and SameSite.

objects.definition: typedef struct http_pause_handle_s http_pause_handle_s;
objects.description: Opaque handle used after pausing an HTTP request; valid only for resumption and udata access.

objects.definition: typedef struct ws_s ws_s;
objects.description: Opaque WebSocket connection handle used within websocket callbacks.
Named-argument struct for websocket upgrade/connect callbacks and user data.
EventSource (SSE) handle type and its settings/callback container. Used for upgrading and handling SSE connections.

objects.definition: typedef fio_url_s http_url_s __attribute__((deprecated("use fio_url_s instead")));
objects.description: Deprecated alias for fio_url_s representing parsed URL components. No definition here beyond typedef.
Named-argument struct for http_sse_subscribe, describing channel, callbacks, udata, and pattern match function.
Named-argument struct for composing an SSE event sent via http_sse_write.

Configuration object for subscribing a websocket to a pub/sub channel. Holds the target websocket, channel, optional callbacks for handling messages and unsubscribe cleanup, user data, pattern matcher, and flags controlling text/binary forwarding behavior.
Forward-declared or externally defined protocol struct type referenced by this header. It is not defined here; only used as a pointer for creating/destroying an HTTP/1.1 protocol instance.
Settings/configuration struct for HTTP handling. It is only referenced in this header as an argument to http1_new and defined elsewhere.
Generic pointer type used for unread data buffer in constructor. Built-in type; included here only because it appears in the API but it is not a custom type defined in this header.
VTable pointer type returned by http1_vtable. Built-in type; not a custom type defined here.

Holds configuration parameters for creating a Redis-backed pub/sub engine instance, including server address, port, optional authentication, and a ping interval. Details about fio_str_info_s come from external headers and are not defined here.

functions.name: fio_malloc
functions.description: Allocates zeroed memory from facil.io’s per-CPU memory pool (or mmap for large allocations). Optimized for short-lived, small objects; memory is 16-byte aligned. Use fio_free to deallocate.
requirements: size may be any non-negative value; allocation of 0 may return non-NULL or NULL depending on implementation
Caller must free with fio_free (or matching deallocator)
Not ideal for long-lived allocations (may cause block fragmentation)

functions.name: fio_calloc
functions.description: Allocates zeroed memory for unit_count units of size_per_unit from facil.io’s pool (or mmap for large). Equivalent to fio_malloc(size_per_unit * unit_count).
requirements: size_per_unit * unit_count may overflow; caller should ensure the product fits size_t
Free with fio_free

functions.name: fio_free
functions.description: Frees memory allocated by facil.io allocation APIs (fio_malloc/fio_calloc/fio_realloc/fio_realloc2/fio_mmap).
requirements: ptr must be a pointer returned by this library’s allocators, or NULL
Do not double-free

functions.name: fio_realloc
functions.description: Reallocates memory; attempts to avoid copying mainly for large allocations (> FIO_MEMORY_BLOCK_ALLOC_LIMIT).
requirements: ptr must be NULL or memory from this allocator
On failure returns NULL without freeing original pointer
new_size is the desired size; may move memory

functions.name: fio_realloc2
functions.description: Reallocates memory with a possible optimization by limiting how much existing data is copied (copy_length).
requirements: ptr must be NULL or memory from this allocator
On failure returns NULL and does not free ptr
copy_length indicates how many bytes to preserve; caller must ensure it does not exceed old size

functions.name: fio_mmap
functions.description: Allocates memory using mmap directly. Suitable for larger, longer-lived objects; fio_free can deallocate it.
requirements: size must be > 0
Free using fio_free

functions.name: fio_malloc_after_fork
functions.description: Resets facil.io allocator locks after the process calls fork() manually. Call in the child post-fork.
requirements: Call in child processes after fork when using the custom allocator
No arguments; safe to call before any further allocator use in child

functions.name: FIO_LOG2STDERR
functions.description: Weak logging sink that writes a formatted message plus newline to stderr, truncating if it exceeds FIO_LOG_LENGTH_LIMIT. Used by FIO_LOG_* macros.
requirements: format must be a printf-style format string
Variadic args must match format
Not thread-safe beyond its internal use; intended as a simple sink

functions.name: fio_attach
functions.description: Attaches (or updates) a protocol object to a socket identified by uuid. Passing NULL detaches (hijacks) the socket. Schedules old protocol’s on_close; on error calls new protocol’s on_close immediately.
requirements: uuid must refer to a valid connection when facil.io is running
protocol may be NULL to detach; otherwise must point to a valid fio_protocol_s
Protocol callbacks must be safe under facil.io’s concurrency model (see struct docs)

functions.name: fio_attach_fd
functions.description: Attaches a protocol to an existing file descriptor and registers it with facil.io. Passing NULL detaches/hijacks. On error, new protocol’s on_close is called immediately.
requirements: fd must be a valid open fd
fd should be set non-blocking and O_CLOEXEC before attaching (see fio_set_non_block)
protocol may be NULL to detach; otherwise valid pointer

functions.name: fio_set_non_block
functions.description: Sets a file descriptor to non-blocking mode and O_CLOEXEC.
requirements: fd must be a valid open fd
Returns OS status; caller should check return and errno

functions.name: fio_capa
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of open connections facil.io can handle per worker process. Returns 0 if uninitialized or resources were released.

functions.name: fio_timeout_set
functions.description: Sets the per-connection timeout in seconds (only when running and connection valid).
requirements: uuid must refer to a valid, running connection
timeout is a small integer (0 means no timeout)

functions.name: fio_timeout_get
functions.description: Gets the per-connection timeout value; returns 0 if none.
requirements: uuid should refer to a current connection; 0 returned if none

functions.name: fio_touch
functions.description: Resets a connection’s timeout counter (“touches” it).
requirements: uuid must refer to a valid connection

functions.name: fio_force_event
functions.signature: void fio_force_event(intptr_t uuid, enum fio_io_event event);
functions.description: Schedules an IO event (on_data, on_ready, or on_timeout) even if it did not occur.
requirements: uuid must refer to a valid socket for effect
event must be one of fio_io_event enum values

functions.name: fio_suspend
functions.description: Temporarily prevents on_data events from firing for a connection until rescheduled (e.g., buffer full or fio_force_event with FIO_EVENT_ON_DATA).
requirements: Should be called within the connection’s on_data callback or when uuid refers to a valid socket; may quietly fail otherwise

functions.name: fio_listen
functions.description: Creates and registers a listening socket/service. on_open is called for each accepted connection; you should attach a protocol with fio_attach or close the uuid. Returns the listening socket uuid or -1 on error.
requirements: args.on_open should be provided and must attach or close uuid
args.port may be NULL (defaults to "3000")
If args.tls is used, it must point to a valid TLS object compatible with facil.io (from fio_tls.h)
on_start/on_finish callbacks must be safe to run in worker processes

functions.name: fio_connect
functions.description: Creates a non-blocking client connection and returns the new socket uuid (or -1 on error). Invokes on_connect on success (should attach a protocol) or on_fail on failure.
requirements: args.address and args.port should specify the remote peer
args.on_connect must handle attaching a protocol or closing the uuid
If args.timeout set, connection failure is assumed after that period
args.tls (if provided) must be a valid TLS object

functions.name: fio_url_parse
functions.description: Parses a URI/URL into components without decoding. Fields reference slices in the original string (not NUL-terminated). Accepts multiple forms (path-only, host:port, user:pass@host, scheme://...).
requirements: url must point to a buffer of at least length bytes
Returned fields are non-owning views; original buffer must remain valid
Invalid formats may produce unexpected results; no error reporting

functions.name: fio_start
functions.description: Starts the facil.io event loop and blocks until shutdown. Spawns threads/processes per args (smart defaults for <=0 values).
requirements: Call after configuring listeners/connectors as needed
Blocks the calling thread until stopped (SIGINT/SIGTERM or fio_stop)

functions.name: fio_stop
functions.description: Attempts to stop the facil.io application (works from master/root process; workers will respawn).
requirements: Must be called in the master/root process to take effect

functions.name: fio_expected_concurrency
functions.description: Returns the expected threads and workers counts via the provided pointers, overwriting their values.
requirements: threads and workers must be valid non-NULL pointers
Pass initial values that match what was passed to fio_start for accurate adjustments

functions.name: fio_is_running
functions.description: Returns the number of worker processes if running (1 in single-process mode), else 0 if not running.

functions.name: fio_is_worker
functions.description: Returns 1 if current process is a worker or a single-process instance, else 0.

functions.name: fio_is_master
functions.description: Returns 1 if current process is the master (root) process, else 0.

functions.name: fio_parent_pid
functions.description: Returns facil.io’s parent (root) process PID.

functions.name: fio_reap_children
functions.description: Enables zombie reaping for the process; call before fio_start to enable global child reaping.
requirements: Call before fio_start to affect global behavior

functions.name: fio_signal_handler_reset
functions.description: Resets signal handlers to their state before facil.io set them. Stops child reaping and default facil.io signal handling. Called automatically on stop.

functions.name: fio_last_tick
functions.description: Returns the last time the server reviewed pending IO events.

functions.name: fio_engine
functions.description: Returns a string naming the selected IO engine: "kqueue", "epoll", or "poll".

functions.name: fio_socket
functions.signature: intptr_t fio_socket(const char *address, const char *port, uint8_t is_server);
functions.description: Creates a Unix or TCP/IP socket and returns its unique facil.io uuid, or -1 on error. For TCP server sockets, address NULL is recommended; for Unix sockets set port to NULL/0.
requirements: For clients, both address and port must specify remote endpoint (unless Unix domain)
For Unix sockets, port must be NULL/0
Returned uuid can be converted to fd via fio_uuid2fd
Does not attach to reactor by itself

functions.name: fio_accept
functions.description: Accepts a new connection from a server socket (created with is_server=1), returning the new connection’s uuid. The new fd is set non-blocking and O_CLOEXEC. Does not attach; use fio_attach.
requirements: srv_uuid must refer to a valid listening socket uuid

functions.name: fio_is_valid
functions.description: Returns 1 if uuid refers to a valid, open socket; 0 otherwise.

functions.name: fio_is_closed
functions.description: Returns 1 if uuid is invalid or socket is flagged to be closed; 0 if valid and open.

functions.name: fio_close
functions.description: Marks the connection to close after pending data is sent. Schedules flush automatically.
requirements: uuid must refer to a connection; safe to call multiple times

functions.name: fio_force_close
functions.description: Immediately closes a connection without protocol restrictions and without sending remaining buffered data.
requirements: uuid should refer to a connection; may drop unsent data

functions.name: fio_peer_addr
functions.description: Returns peer address info for a socket. If unavailable, data==NULL in result. Available when socket was accepted via fio_accept or opened using fio_connect.
requirements: uuid should be a valid connection; otherwise returned .data may be NULL

functions.name: fio_local_addr
functions.description: Writes the local machine’s address (qualified host name) to dest. Returns bytes written (excluding NUL). If return equals limit-1 output may be truncated.
requirements: dest must point to a buffer of at least limit bytes
limit must be > 0
On error returns 0 and errno may be set; dest contents undefined

functions.name: fio_read
functions.signature: ssize_t fio_read(intptr_t uuid, void *buffer, size_t count);
functions.description: Reads up to count bytes from the connection into buffer. Returns number of bytes read (0 means no data), or -1 on fatal error/closed connection. Semantics differ from native read to simplify usage; transport layers may delay availability.
requirements: uuid must be a valid connection
buffer must be a valid writable memory of at least count bytes

functions.name: fio_write2_fn
functions.description: Schedules data to be written to the socket using flexible options (buffer or file descriptor, offsets, length, deallocation callback, urgent). Ownership of data moves to socket; deallocated via .after callback or default.
requirements: uuid must be a valid connection
If options.is_fd==1, options.data.fd must be a valid file descriptor
If options.is_fd==0, options.data.buffer must point to at least options.length bytes
If .after.dealloc is provided, it must not call socket APIs (may deadlock)
offset and length must not exceed source size/file length intended

functions.name: FIO_DEALLOC_NOOP
functions.description: No-op deallocation callback for fio_write2 when no deallocation is required.

functions.name: fio_write
functions.signature: ssize_t fio_write(intptr_t uuid, const void *buffer, size_t length);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper that copies length bytes from buffer and schedules sending via fio_write2. Returns -1 on allocation error; 0 on success.
requirements: buffer must point to at least length bytes; length>0
uuid must be valid for data to be eventually sent

functions.name: fio_sendfile
functions.signature: ssize_t fio_sendfile(intptr_t uuid, intptr_t source_fd, off_t offset, size_t length);
functions.description: Schedules sending a file (or slice) as a single logical packet. Closes source_fd when finished. May use sendfile when possible; otherwise buffered chunking is used.
requirements: source_fd must be a valid open file descriptor positioned arbitrarily (offset supplied)
offset and length define the slice; length 0 means send 0 bytes
On error returns -1 and the file is closed

functions.name: fio_pending
functions.description: Returns the number of queued fio_write calls not yet processed for the socket.
requirements: uuid should be a valid connection

functions.name: fio_flush
functions.description: Attempts to flush internal buffers to the socket and close if marked and drained. Returns 1 if data remains, 0 if drained, -1 on error/closed. Sets errno=EWOULDBLOCK if socket’s lock is busy.
requirements: uuid should be a valid connection
Caller should handle EWOULDBLOCK (e.g., retry or use fio_flush_strong)

functions.name: fio_flush_all
functions.description: Attempts to flush all open connections. Returns the number of sockets still needing flush.

functions.name: fio_fd2uuid
functions.description: Returns the active uuid for an existing file descriptor. If the fd was closed, it may be registered as open (false positives possible until registry updates). Returns -1 on error.
requirements: fd must be a non-negative file descriptor
If fd wasn’t opened/registered with facil.io (in the second variant described), function returns -1

functions.name: fio_uuid_link
functions.description: Links an object to a connection’s lifetime; on connection close, on_close(obj) is called with high priority. If uuid invalid, on_close is called immediately.
requirements: uuid may be invalid; expect immediate on_close in that case
on_close must be non-NULL and must be fast (long tasks should be deferred)
obj is opaque to facil.io; must remain valid until callback

functions.name: fio_uuid_unlink
functions.description: Unlinks a previously linked object so its on_close won’t be called. Returns 0 on success, -1 if object not found; errno set to EBADF for invalid uuid or ENOTCONN if object wasn’t linked.
requirements: uuid should refer to a valid connection
obj must be the exact pointer used in link
Caller should check errno on failure

functions.name: fio_rw_hook_set
functions.description: Sets read/write hook functions (replacing system recv/write) for a socket. The hooks must not call facil.io APIs; they can manage internal buffers and flush. Cleanup will be called when socket closes or hook replaced.
requirements: uuid must be valid
rw_hooks must point to a valid fio_rw_hook_s struct (or NULL to clear to defaults)
Hooks must not call facil.io socket APIs (risk of deadlock)
udata is opaque and passed to hooks

functions.name: fio_rw_hook_replace_unsafe
functions.description: Replaces existing read/write hook from within a read/write hook callback. Does not call cleanup of the old hook. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: Should only be called from within an existing r/w hook callback (unsafe otherwise)
Hooks must not call facil.io socket APIs

functions.name: fio_fork
functions.description: Override point for fork; behaves like system fork().
requirements: If overridden, must mimic POSIX fork semantics (return values, duplicated state)

functions.name: fio_thread_new
functions.description: Override point to create a new thread running thread_func(arg). Returns an identifier pointer for the thread, or NULL on error. Must allocate memory for the thread identifier.
requirements: thread_func must be a valid function pointer
If overridden, must allocate and return an identifier to be later freed/joined

functions.name: fio_thread_free
functions.description: Override point to free memory associated with a thread identifier, without joining or stopping the thread.
requirements: p_thr must be a thread identifier previously returned by fio_thread_new

functions.name: fio_thread_join
functions.description: Override point to join a thread identified by p_thr. Should also free any allocated memory. Return value is ignored.
requirements: p_thr must be an identifier previously returned by fio_thread_new

functions.name: fio_defer_io_task
functions.description: Schedules a protected per-connection task to run under the connection’s lock. If the connection closes before execution, args.fallback is called.
requirements: args.task must be provided
uuid should refer to a connection for the task to run; otherwise fallback runs if provided
args.type controls lock level (TASK/WRITE)

functions.name: fio_defer
functions.description: Defers a generic task for later execution. The task takes two opaque pointers. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: task must be non-NULL and safe to run later
udata pointers must remain valid or refer to durable allocations if needed

functions.name: fio_run_every
functions.signature: int fio_run_every(size_t milliseconds, size_t repetitions, void (*task)(void *), void *arg, void (*on_finish)(void *));
functions.description: Creates a repeating timer to run task(arg) every interval. Repeats 'repetitions' times (0 means forever). Returns -1 on error. on_finish is always called (even on error).
requirements: task must be non-NULL
milliseconds is the interval; large values supported
on_finish may be NULL; if non-NULL must be safe to call once timer stops

functions.name: fio_defer_perform
functions.description: Performs all deferred tasks that are pending.

functions.name: fio_defer_has_queue
functions.description: Returns non-zero if there are deferred functions waiting to execute.

functions.name: fio_state_callback_add
functions.description: Registers a process/state callback for a specific lifecycle event (initialize, start, fork hooks, idle, shutdown, finish, crash notifications, at_exit).
requirements: func must be non-NULL
arg is opaque and passed to callback
Safe to register multiple callbacks; order is LIFO on force

functions.name: fio_state_callback_remove
functions.description: Unregisters a previously added state callback. Returns 0 on success, non-zero if not found.
requirements: type, func, and arg must match the added callback

functions.name: fio_state_callback_force

functions.name: fio_state_callback_clear

functions.name: fio_ct_true

key1/key2 must be secret keys for security

functions.name: fio_sha1

functions.name: fio_sha2_512

data may be NULL only if len==0

functions.name: fio_sha2_256
functions.description: Helper to compute SHA-2 (SHA_256 variant) over data; initializes, writes, and finalizes.

data may be NULL only if len==0

functions.name: fio_sha2_384

functions.name: fio_test

functions.name: fio_str_new2

functions.name: fio_str_new_copy2

functions.name: fio_str_dup

functions.name: fio_str_free

requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a fio_str_s container

functions.name: fio_str_free2
functions.description: Frees the string’s resources and the container itself (using fio_free).
requirements: s must have been allocated with fio_str_new2 or fio_malloc
After call, s pointer is invalid

functions.name: fio_str_send_free2
functions.description: Sends a fio_str_s via fio_write2 and frees both the string data and its container once sent.
requirements: uuid must be a valid connection
str must be a heap-allocated fio_str_s (fio_str_new2/fio_malloc)
Do not use str after scheduling

functions.name: fio_str_detach
functions.description: Detaches the string data from the container, returning a heap buffer with a NUL terminator and clearing the container to an empty state. Caller must free the returned buffer.
requirements: s must be valid
Returned pointer must be freed with fio_free
After detaching, s remains valid but empty

functions.name: fio_str_info
functions.description: Returns a struct with capacity, length, and data pointer for the string. For small/inline strings, capacity is 0 if frozen or small-capacity-1 otherwise; data points to internal buffer.
requirements: s may be NULL; returns zeros in that case
Returned data pointer is non-owning; valid as long as string isn’t reallocated

functions.name: fio_str_len
functions.description: Returns the string’s length in bytes.
requirements: s must be valid

functions.name: fio_str_data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the string’s data (mutable unless frozen).
requirements: s must be valid
Do not write when s is frozen

functions.name: fio_str_capa
functions.description: Returns current capacity (including used and free space). Returns 0 if frozen.
requirements: s must be valid

functions.name: fio_str_resize
functions.description: Changes the string’s length without reallocating beyond existing capacity when possible; extends capacity as needed. When shrinking, data beyond new size may be corrupted. Writes a trailing NUL.
requirements: s must be valid and not frozen
size must fit memory; may allocate
When expanding beyond capacity, existing data beyond old len may be replaced with NUL bytes

functions.name: fio_str_hash
functions.description: Returns the string’s current Risky Hash value (implementation may change).
requirements: s must be valid; result not suitable for cryptographic purposes

functions.name: fio_str_compact
functions.description: Attempts to minimize memory by shrinking allocations or storing small strings inline. Effects depend on allocator.
requirements: s must be valid

functions.name: fio_str_capa_assert
functions.description: Ensures the string has at least needed capacity, reallocating or moving from inline to heap as necessary. Returns current state.
requirements: s must be valid and not frozen

functions.name: fio_str_utf8_valid
functions.description: Returns 1 if the string content is valid UTF-8, 0 otherwise.
requirements: s must be valid

functions.name: fio_str_utf8_len
functions.description: Returns the number of UTF-8 code points in the string if valid; returns 0 on invalid UTF-8.
requirements: s must be valid

functions.name: fio_str_utf8_select
functions.description: Given a UTF-8 character selection (pos, len in code points), updates pos/len to byte offsets into the string. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error (pos set to -1).
requirements: s must be valid
pos and len must be valid pointers
Negative pos counts from end (-1=end)

functions.name: fio_str_write

functions.description: Appends raw bytes to the end of the string, extending capacity as needed.
requirements: s must be valid and not frozen
src must point to at least src_len bytes (src_len>0)

functions.name: fio_str_write_i
functions.description: Appends a signed integer in base-10 textual form to the string.
requirements: s must be valid and not frozen

functions.name: fio_str_concat
functions.description: Appends src’s bytes to dest.
requirements: dest must be valid and not frozen
src must be valid; if empty, no change

functions.name: fio_str_replace
functions.signature: fio_str_info_s fio_str_replace(fio_str_s *s, intptr_t start_pos, size_t old_len, const void *src, size_t src_len);
functions.description: Replaces old_len bytes at start_pos with src bytes. Negative start_pos counts from end (-1=end). Insertion when old_len==0, deletion when src_len==0.
requirements: s must be valid and not frozen
start_pos may be negative (relative)
If replacement exceeds end, behaves like append from start_pos

functions.name: fio_str_vprintf

format must be a printf-style format string
argv must be a valid va_list

functions.name: fio_str_printf
functions.description: Appends formatted text (printf-style) to the string.
requirements: s must be valid and not frozen
format must be a printf-style format string
Variadic arguments must match format

functions.name: fio_str_readfile

functions.description: Reads a file (or slice) and appends its contents to s. On error, returns state with data==NULL. POSIX-only.

On failure, s is restored and returned state has data==NULL

functions.name: fio_str_freeze
functions.description: Marks the string as frozen, preventing further modifications.

functions.name: fio_str_iseq
functions.description: Binary equality comparison. Returns 1 if equal length and bytes, else 0.

functions.name: fiobj_null
functions.description: Returns the FIOBJ null sentinel. Intended to represent a NULL-like value in the dynamic object system.

functions.name: fiobj_true
functions.description: Returns the FIOBJ boolean true sentinel.

functions.name: fiobj_false
functions.description: Returns the FIOBJ boolean false sentinel.
requirements: No arguments.

functions.name: fiobj_type_name
functions.description: Returns a C string naming the object's dynamic type. For allocated objects it uses the vtable class_name; for primitives/numbers it returns a literal string.
requirements: Argument o may be any FIOBJ value, including 0.

functions.name: fiobj_dup
functions.description: Heuristic copy by reference. Increments the reference count for allocated objects (and any nested objects) and returns the same FIOBJ value.
requirements: It is safe to pass any FIOBJ (allocated, primitive, or null).
Caller must eventually balance with fiobj_free for allocated objects to release resources.

functions.name: fiobj_free
functions.description: Decrements an object's reference count and releases memory/resources when the count reaches zero. For container types (arrays/hashes), nested objects are also freed. Note: despite an earlier comment mentioning a numeric return, this function returns void.
requirements: It is safe to pass any FIOBJ; non-allocated/primitives are ignored.
Must not be called concurrently on the same object without external synchronization beyond the provided atomic refcount semantics for the ref field.

functions.name: fiobj_is_true
functions.description: Tests if an object evaluates as true according to its type semantics (e.g., empty strings may evaluate to false, true/false sentinels evaluate accordingly, numbers are true if non-zero).
requirements: Argument o may be any FIOBJ value, including primitives and 0.

functions.name: fiobj_obj2num

functions.name: fiobj_obj2float

functions.name: fiobj_mustache_load
functions.description: Loads and parses a Mustache template from a file, producing an opaque mustache_s instruction array for later rendering. Use when you have a file path (and length) in a fio_str_info_s. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: filename must reference a valid file name string (and length) representing the root template to load.

functions.name: fiobj_mustache_new
functions.description: Creates a Mustache template from either a file or in-memory data, returning an opaque mustache_s instruction array. Accepts named initializer fields via mustache_load_args_s (filename/filename_len, data/data_len, err). Returns NULL on error. The variadic macro wrapper allows convenient designated-initializer style calls.

If providing err, it must point to a writable mustache_error_en to receive error details (see mustache_parser.h).
The returned mustache_s* must be freed with fiobj_mustache_free when no longer needed.
Callers using the macro form must use designated initializers compatible with mustache_load_args_s (e.g., .filename=..., .filename_len=...).

functions.name: fiobj_mustache_free
functions.description: Releases all resources associated with a mustache_s template previously created by fiobj_mustache_load or fiobj_mustache_new.
requirements: mustache must be a pointer returned by fiobj_mustache_load or fiobj_mustache_new.

Behavior for NULL is unknown; pass a valid pointer.

functions.name: fiobj_mustache_build
functions.description: Renders a Mustache template into a newly created FIOBJ String using the provided data object. On success returns the resulting FIOBJ String; on failure returns FIOBJ_INVALID.

functions.name: fiobj_json2obj

functions.description: Parses a JSON document from the provided buffer and, on success, sets *pobj to a newly created FIOBJ representing the parsed value. Returns the number of bytes consumed from data (allowing incremental parsing). Returns 0 on error and consumes no input. Caller is responsible for freeing the created object. JSON nesting is limited by JSON_MAX_DEPTH (32).

len must correctly reflect the number of bytes available in data.

On error (return 0), *pobj is not modified and the caller must not attempt to free it based on this call’s result.

pretty is a boolean-like flag; 0 for compact output, non-zero for pretty-printed output.

Caller must free as usual. pretty controls compact vs. pretty-printed formatting. Only basic FIOBJ types are supported; unsupported types may be formatted incorrectly.

object should be one of the supported basic FIOBJ types (primitive, number, float, string, hash, or array) for correct output; other types are unsupported and may yield incorrect formatting.

requirements: If len > 0, data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory (non-NULL).

key1 and key2 must be initialized 64-bit values; typically kept secret and consistent for a hashing domain.

requirements: If len > 0, data must point to at least len bytes of readable memory (non-NULL).

key1 and key2 must be initialized 64-bit values; typically kept secret and consistent for a hashing domain.

functions.name: fio_tmpfile
functions.description: Creates a new temporary file using mkstemp in the system temporary directory (P_tmpdir if defined and writable, otherwise /tmp). Returns the open POSIX file descriptor for the created file, or -1 on failure. The filename is not returned or stored; only the descriptor is provided. Typical usage is to obtain an fd for temporary read/write I/O. Note: because the path is not exposed and the function does not unlink the file, the temporary file remains linked in the filesystem after close unless the caller takes extra measures outside this API.
requirements: Caller must check the return value: fd >= 0 indicates success; a return of -1 indicates failure and errno provides the error cause.
On success, the returned descriptor must be closed with close(fd) when no longer needed to avoid descriptor leaks.
The function must be run in an environment where the chosen temporary directory (P_tmpdir or /tmp) exists and is writable by the process, otherwise mkstemp will fail.
The returned value is a POSIX file descriptor (int), not a FILE*; do not pass it to stdio functions unless you convert it (e.g., via fdopen).

This API does not expose the generated pathname and does not unlink the file; if your application requires removing the file from the filesystem, you must arrange cleanup via external means (e.g., track the path separately in another API) or use a different helper that unlinks after creation.

functions.name: fiobj_send_free
functions.signature: static inline __attribute__((unused)) ssize_t fiobj_send_free(intptr_t uuid, FIOBJ o);
functions.description: Enqueue a zero-copy write of the bytes represented by the given FIOBJ to the socket/connection identified by uuid, and free the object after the write completes. Internally converts the object to a C-string view (fiobj_obj2cstr), computes an offset into the object’s allocation for the data pointer, and calls fio_write2 with a deallocation callback that fiobj_free’s the object. Use this to send a FIOBJ string-like buffer without copying and without needing to manually free it afterwards. Unknowns: exact semantics and error codes of fio_write2; which FIOBJ types are guaranteed to have data co-located with the object for valid offset computation.
requirements: uuid must refer to a valid, open socket/connection recognized by fio_write2.
o must be a valid, initialized FIOBJ and must not be NULL.

o must be a FIOBJ string-like/data object where fiobj_obj2cstr(o).data points inside the same allocation as o (so the computed offset is valid). Passing other object types may result in undefined behavior.
Caller must not access or reuse o after calling, as it will be freed asynchronously via the write-completion deallocator.
Caller should check the returned ssize_t from fio_write2 semantics (negative on error; exact values depend on the sock library).

Function may queue an asynchronous write; the data memory (o) must remain valid until the write completes. This function arranges that by passing o along with a dealloc callback; do not free o manually.

functions.name: fio_cli_start
functions.signature: void fio_cli_start(int argc, char const *argv[], int unnamed_min, int unnamed_max, char const *description, char const **names);
functions.description: Initializes and parses command-line arguments into an internal dictionary for easy access by name/alias and position. Expected usage is via the fio_cli_start(...) macro, which appends a required NULL terminator to the names list and supports inline type/print specifiers (FIO_CLI_STRING/BOOL/INT/PRINT/PRINT_HEADER). Use this before calling any accessors (fio_cli_get, fio_cli_get_i, fio_cli_unnamed, etc.) and call fio_cli_end when finished. This call is not thread safe.

Argument names in the names list must start with '-' and the first non '-' token that follows begins that argument's description.
Unnamed arguments must not be listed among the named arguments.
The named arguments list (names) must be NULL-terminated (the macro ensures this).
Type specifiers are optional; when used, they must be one of FIO_CLI_STRING, FIO_CLI_BOOL, FIO_CLI_INT, FIO_CLI_PRINT, or FIO_CLI_PRINT_HEADER accompanying a description line.
If a provided argument fails a declared type requirement, execution will end and an error plus help text will be printed.
This function is not thread safe; do not call concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: fio_cli_end
functions.description: Releases all memory used by the internal CLI dictionary created by fio_cli_start. Call this after you finish accessing parsed arguments.
requirements: Should be called after a successful fio_cli_start to free resources associated with parsing.
This function is not thread safe; do not call concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: fio_cli_get
functions.description: Returns the parsed value for a named CLI argument as a NUL-terminated C string, or NULL if the argument was not provided.
requirements: name must be a valid argument identifier (argument names must start with '-') as defined when calling fio_cli_start.
Must be called after fio_cli_start has successfully parsed the CLI and before fio_cli_end frees the data.

functions.name: fio_cli_get_i
functions.description: Returns the parsed value for a named CLI argument converted to an integer. If the argument was not provided or not an integer, behavior follows the library’s internal parsing rules (not specified here).
requirements: name must be a valid argument identifier (argument names must start with '-') as defined when calling fio_cli_start.
The argument should satisfy any integer type requirement declared for it; otherwise the start phase would have already printed an error and terminated.
Must be called after fio_cli_start has successfully parsed the CLI and before fio_cli_end.

functions.name: fio_cli_unnamed_count

requirements: Must be called after fio_cli_start has successfully parsed the CLI and before fio_cli_end.

functions.name: fio_cli_unnamed
functions.description: Returns the unnamed (positional) argument string at the given 0-based index, or NULL if out of range.
requirements: index is 0-based.
Must be called after fio_cli_start has successfully parsed the CLI and before fio_cli_end.

functions.name: fio_cli_set
functions.description: Manually sets the value of a named CLI argument to the provided NUL-terminated C string without copying. This does not check aliases or type constraints and only affects the specific name provided.
requirements: name must match the exact key under which the value should be stored; aliases are not automatically linked.
value is not copied and must remain valid (memory must stay alive) until fio_cli_end is called.
May violate declared type requirements; callers are responsible for ensuring consistency.
Must be used after fio_cli_start initializes the CLI state and before fio_cli_end frees it.

protocol_name must be non-NULL and name the ALPN protocol to register
on_selected may be NULL
