requirements: uuid must be a valid socket UUID already connected to a peer (e.g., provided to an on_connect callback of fio_connect)
tls must be a valid fio_tls_s pointer configured as desired (server_name/certificates/ALPN/trust as needed)
udata may be NULL

functions.name: fio_tls_dup
functions.description: Increases the reference count of the TLS object. Each increment must be paired with a corresponding fio_tls_destroy to release the reference.
requirements: tls must be a valid fio_tls_s pointer
Each call to fio_tls_dup must be balanced by a later call to fio_tls_destroy to avoid leaks

functions.name: fio_tls_destroy
functions.description: Decreases the reference count and, when it reaches zero, destroys the TLS context and frees associated resources. Triggers ALPN on_cleanup callbacks for registered protocols.
requirements: tls must be a valid fio_tls_s pointer (or NULL behavior is unknown)
Every reference obtained (including the original from fio_tls_new and any added via fio_tls_dup) must be released with fio_tls_destroy

functions.name: http_set_header
functions.signature: int http_set_header(http_s *h, FIOBJ name, FIOBJ value);
functions.description: Sets a response header on the given HTTP handle. Takes ownership of the value object but not the name object, allowing name reuse. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. Use within the lifetime of a valid http_s in an on_request/on_response or deferred context.
requirements: h must be a valid, not-yet-finished http_s handle and only accessed within on_request/on_response callbacks or an http_defer callback.
name must be a valid FIOBJ representing the header name; caller retains ownership of name.
value must be a valid FIOBJ representing the header value; ownership is transferred to the HTTP object.
Must be called before the response is sent (before http_send_body/http_sendfile/http_finish).
Caller should check return value for errors (-1).

functions.name: http_set_header2
functions.signature: int http_set_header2(http_s *h, fio_str_info_s name, fio_str_info_s value);
functions.description: Sets a response header using lightweight string views (fio_str_info_s) for name and value. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: h must be a valid, not-yet-finished http_s handle and only accessed within on_request/on_response callbacks or an http_defer callback.
name and value must reference valid memory for the duration of the call; they are copied internally.
Must be called before the response is sent.
Caller should check return value for errors (-1).

functions.name: http_set_cookie
functions.description: Sets a Set-Cookie response header using the provided cookie arguments (supports attributes such as Max-Age, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Partitioned). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. A macro variant allows designated/named arguments.
requirements: h must be a valid, not-yet-finished http_s handle and only accessed within on_request/on_response callbacks or an http_defer callback.
Cookie name/value length must not be excessively long; long names/values are treated as a security violation and return an error.
Must be called before the response is sent.
Caller should check return value for errors (-1).

functions.name: http_send_body
functions.description: Sends response headers and a body payload from memory. The body data is copied to the HTTP stream; the caller remains responsible for freeing the original buffer. On success returns 0; -1 on error. After a successful call, the http_s handle becomes invalid.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle and only accessed within the allowed callback/task context.
data must point to at least length bytes of readable memory.
Must not be used after another terminal response call (e.g., http_sendfile/http_finish).
After a successful call, h is invalid and must not be used further.
Caller should check return value for errors (-1) and free data if needed.

functions.name: http_sendfile
functions.signature: int http_sendfile(http_s *h, int fd, uintptr_t length, uintptr_t offset);
functions.description: Sends response headers and uses an open file descriptor as the response body. The file descriptor is closed automatically. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. After a successful call, the http_s handle becomes invalid.
requirements: h must be valid and used only within permitted callback/task context.
fd must be a valid open file descriptor positioned appropriately; it will be closed by this function.
length defines the number of bytes to send starting at offset (if supported by platform).
Must be called only once per response and before any other terminal send call.
After a successful call, h is invalid and must not be used.
Caller must check return value for -1.

functions.name: http_sendfile2
functions.signature: int http_sendfile2(http_s *h, const char *prefix, size_t prefix_len, const char *encoded, size_t encoded_len);
functions.description: Sends response headers and serves a file computed by joining a raw prefix with a URL-decoded encoded path component. Either or both strings may be empty. Returns 0 on success (and consumes the http_s handle) or -1 on error (handle remains valid).
requirements: h must be valid and used only within permitted callback/task context.
prefix and encoded must point to valid memory of the given lengths; encoded is URL-decoded internally, prefix is used as-is.
On success, h is consumed/invalidated; on error, h remains usable.
Caller must check return value for 0/-1.

functions.name: http_send_error
functions.description: Sends an HTTP error response with the given status code (e.g., 404, 500). Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. After sending, the http_s handle is invalid. If h is NULL, additional internal details (uuid/settings) would be required, but this header exposes only the simplified form.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle or NULL; when NULL, the implementation may require extra context (not exposed here).
error_code should be a valid HTTP status code (e.g., 400–599).
After a successful call, h is invalid and must not be used.
Caller must check return value for -1.

functions.name: http_finish
functions.description: Sends only the response headers and finishes the HTTP response without a body (header-only response). After this call, the http_s handle becomes invalid.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle and used only within the allowed callback/task context.
Must be called at most once per response and not after another terminal send call.
After the call, h must not be used.

functions.name: http_push_data
functions.signature: int http_push_data(http_s *h, void *data, uintptr_t length, FIOBJ mime_type);
functions.description: Attempts HTTP/2 server push of a data payload with an optional MIME type hint. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. Only meaningful on HTTP/2 connections that support push.
requirements: h must be valid and on a connection that supports HTTP/2 push.
data must point to at least length bytes; data may be copied internally; caller remains responsible for original buffer lifecycle unless documented otherwise.
mime_type may be NULL to omit the hint (behavior depends on implementation).
Caller must check return value for -1.

functions.name: http_push_file
functions.signature: int http_push_file(http_s *h, FIOBJ filename, FIOBJ mime_type);
functions.description: Attempts HTTP/2 server push of a file. If mime_type is NULL, the type may be auto-detected from the filename. Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
requirements: h must be valid and on a connection that supports HTTP/2 push.
filename must be a valid FIOBJ String referencing a path; caller manages its lifecycle as per FIOBJ rules unless consumed.
mime_type may be NULL to trigger auto-detection.
Caller must check return value for -1.

functions.name: http_pause
functions.description: Pauses HTTP handling for the current request/response and invalidates the current http_s handle. Schedules the provided task, receiving an opaque pause handle to resume later using http_resume.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle used within an allowed callback/task context.
After calling, the given http_s becomes invalid and must not be accessed.
task must be a valid function pointer; it will be invoked with an http_pause_handle_s* usable only for a single http_resume call.
The opaque pause handle cannot be used with any http_* API except http_resume and paused udata accessors.

functions.name: http_resume
functions.description: Resumes a paused HTTP request/response. The provided task receives a fresh http_s handle and must call one of the terminal HTTP functions (http_send_*, http_finish) or http_pause. Optionally, a fallback is called with stored udata if resume cannot proceed.
requirements: http must be the opaque handle received from a prior http_pause; can be used exactly once to resume.
task must not be NULL and must call one of: http_send_*, http_finish, or http_pause.
fallback may be NULL; if provided, it will receive the udata stored in the paused handle for cleanup.
The http_s passed to task is valid only within that task scope; after a terminal call it becomes invalid.

functions.name: http_paused_udata_get
functions.description: Returns the opaque udata pointer associated with a paused HTTP handle.
requirements: http must be a valid http_pause_handle_s previously obtained via http_pause.
May only be used while the request is paused and before/at the time of http_resume.

functions.name: http_paused_udata_set
functions.description: Sets the opaque udata pointer associated with a paused HTTP handle, returning the previous value.
requirements: http must be a valid http_pause_handle_s previously obtained via http_pause.
May only be used while the request is paused and before/at the time of http_resume.

functions.name: http_listen
functions.signature: intptr_t http_listen(const char *port, const char *binding, struct http_settings_s settings);
functions.description: Starts an HTTP server listening on the given port and optional binding address. Returns -1 on error or the listening socket’s uuid on success. The settings.on_finish callback is always called. A macro with the same name exists to allow designated initialization.
requirements: port must be a valid service/port string (e.g., "3000").
binding may be NULL to accept any interface, or a valid address/IFACE string.
settings must be an initialized struct http_settings_s; callbacks such as on_request/on_upgrade may be provided; unprovided fields default as per implementation.
Caller must check for return value -1 to detect errors.

functions.name: http_connect
functions.signature: intptr_t http_connect(const char *url, const char *unix_address, struct http_settings_s settings);
functions.description: Connects as an HTTP client to the target URL (supports full URL with optional path/query). On successful connection, on_response is invoked first with an empty request handle to populate and send; subsequent on_response calls deliver the server’s response. Returns -1 on error or the socket’s uuid on success. A macro variant allows designated settings initialization.
requirements: url must be a valid URL-like string; path and query components, if present, are attached to the http_s path.
unix_address may be NULL or a valid Unix domain socket path depending on transport used.
settings.on_response is required for client mode; other fields optional.
Caller must check for return value -1 to detect errors.

functions.name: http_settings
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the http_settings_s used to configure the connection associated with the given HTTP handle, or NULL on error.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle in scope.
Caller must check for NULL before use of the returned pointer.

functions.name: http_peer_addr
functions.description: Returns a direct address string view for the connected peer (possibly an intermediary).
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle.
The returned fio_str_info_s references memory managed by the library; treat as read-only and use immediately or copy if needed.

functions.name: http_hijack
functions.description: Detaches the underlying socket from the HTTP protocol and facil.io, allowing custom protocol handling. Optionally returns any unread buffered bytes in leftover. Returns the socket’s uuid. After hijack, HTTP parsing may still attempt reads if HTTP functions are mistakenly used.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle.
If leftover is non-NULL and leftover->data is provided by the library, it will be automatically deallocated by the library; copy data if it must persist.
Caller should avoid calling additional HTTP API after hijacking to prevent protocol confusion.

functions.name: http_upgrade2ws
functions.description: Upgrades an HTTP/1.1 connection to a WebSocket connection. Ends the HTTP stage, invalidates the http_s, and sets the WebSocket udata. The client on_finish callback is invoked when HTTP stage completes. Returns 0/implementation-defined success, non-zero on failure (per facil.io conventions often 0 success, -1 error).
requirements: http must be a valid http_s handle representing an upgradeable HTTP/1.1 request.
settings may provide on_message/on_open/on_ready/on_shutdown/on_close and udata; unset callbacks are optional.
After a successful call the http_s is invalid and must not be used.
Caller should check return value for error indication.

functions.name: websocket_connect
functions.description: Connects to a WebSocket service at the provided URL. Minimal client: no built-in auth/logic, intended to be simple. Returns a connection uuid on success, -1 on error.
requirements: url must be a valid WebSocket URL (e.g., ws:// or wss://).
settings may define callbacks and udata; on_close will be invoked with uuid and udata.
Caller must check return value for -1.

functions.name: http_upgrade2sse
functions.description: Upgrades an HTTP connection to an EventSource (SSE) connection. The http_s handle becomes invalid after this call. On HTTP/1.1 this precludes future requests on the same connection.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle on an upgradeable request.
settings may provide on_open/on_ready/on_shutdown/on_close and udata.
After a successful call the http_s is invalid and must not be used.
Caller should check return value for an error (non-zero/negative per implementation).

functions.name: http_sse_set_timout
functions.description: Sets the ping interval (timeout) for an SSE connection. Note: function name contains a spelling typo ‘timout’ in the API.
requirements: sse must be a valid http_sse_s handle.
timeout is in seconds and should be a reasonable small value (defaults in library are around 40s).

functions.name: http_sse_subscribe
functions.description: Subscribes an SSE connection to a pub/sub channel with optional on_message and on_unsubscribe callbacks. Returns a subscription ID on success, 0 on failure. All subscriptions are cleared when the connection closes.
requirements: sse must be a valid http_sse_s handle.
args.channel must reference the channel name; optional callbacks may be NULL.
Caller must check the return value: 0 indicates failure.
To cancel, use http_sse_unsubscribe (not fio_unsubscribe).

functions.name: http_sse_unsubscribe
functions.description: Cancels a subscription created by http_sse_subscribe and invalidates that subscription ID.
requirements: sse must be a valid http_sse_s handle.
subscription must be a valid non-zero ID returned by http_sse_subscribe.
After unsubscription, the ID is invalid and must not be reused.

functions.name: http_sse_write
functions.description: Writes an SSE event to the connection, with optional id, event, data, and retry fields. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: sse must be a valid http_sse_s handle.
args fields (id/event/data) should be valid fio_str_info_s views; retry optional.
Caller must check return value for failure.

functions.name: http_sse2uuid
functions.description: Returns the underlying connection UUID for an SSE handle (useful for scheduling I/O tasks or pub/sub).
requirements: sse must be a valid http_sse_s handle.

functions.name: http_sse_close
functions.description: Closes an EventSource (SSE) connection. Returns implementation-defined status (commonly 0 on success).
requirements: sse must be a valid http_sse_s handle.
Caller should check the return value for errors.

functions.name: http_sse_dup
functions.description: Duplicates an SSE handle by reference, increasing the internal reference count. Returns the same pointer; no allocation is made. Must later be released with http_sse_free.
requirements: sse must be a valid http_sse_s handle.
Each duplication must be balanced by a corresponding http_sse_free call.

functions.name: http_sse_free
functions.description: Decreases the SSE handle’s reference count; frees underlying resources when the count reaches zero.
requirements: sse must be a valid http_sse_s handle obtained from upgrade or duplicated via http_sse_dup.
Do not use sse after it has been freed (when last reference is released).

functions.name: http_parse_body
functions.description: Parses and decodes the request body into h->params based on Content-Type. Supported: application/x-www-form-urlencoded, application/json, multipart/form-data. For JSON non-object roots, stores under key "JSON". Returns 0/implementation-defined; - typical usage is to check success/non-error.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s request handle with a body to parse.
Should be called before http_parse_query to allow JSON data to participate in params.
Caller should check return value for error indication.

functions.name: http_parse_query
functions.description: Parses the URL query string into h->params using http_add2hash semantics. Should be called after http_parse_body.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle.
Call after http_parse_body when JSON bodies may exist.

functions.name: http_parse_cookies
functions.description: Parses Cookie or Set-Cookie headers into h->cookies using http_add2hash conventions. If is_url_encoded is non-zero, values are URL-decoded.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle.
is_url_encoded indicates whether cookie values are URL-encoded.

functions.name: http_add2hash
functions.signature: int http_add2hash(FIOBJ dest, char *name, size_t name_len, char *value, size_t value_len, uint8_t encoded);
functions.description: Adds a named parameter to a Hash object, converting the given C strings to FIOBJ and resolving nested syntax (e.g., name[], name[key], name[][key]). Optionally URL-decodes when encoded is non-zero. Returns 0/implementation-defined or -1 on error per library conventions.
requirements: dest must be a valid FIOBJ Hash to receive parsed data.
name must not start with '[' or end with ']'; name/name_len define the parameter name.
value/value_len define the parameter value string.
encoded non-zero enables URL decoding of value/name where applicable.
Invalid constructs like "name[][]" are considered errors.

functions.name: http_add2hash2
functions.signature: int http_add2hash2(FIOBJ dest, char *name, size_t name_len, FIOBJ value, uint8_t encoded);
functions.description: Adds a named parameter to a Hash object using an existing FIOBJ value, resolving nested syntax in the name similarly to http_add2hash. Optionally treats input as URL-encoded when encoded is non-zero.
requirements: dest must be a valid FIOBJ Hash.
name must not start with '[' or end with ']'; name/name_len define the parameter with nested semantics.
value must be a valid FIOBJ (ownership semantics per library; not specified here).
encoded indicates URL-decoding behavior where applicable.
Constructs like "name[][]" are invalid.

functions.name: http_status2str
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string view describing the given HTTP status code. The view is valid per library’s lifetime guarantees.
requirements: status should be a valid HTTP status integer (e.g., 200, 404).
The returned fio_str_info_s should be treated as read-only; copy if persistence is required.

functions.name: http_mimetype_register
functions.signature: void http_mimetype_register(char *file_ext, size_t file_ext_len, FIOBJ mime_type_str);
functions.description: Registers a MIME type string to be associated with a file extension in the internal registry.
requirements: file_ext must point to the extension bytes (without dot) of length file_ext_len.
mime_type_str must be a valid FIOBJ String representing the MIME type.
Should be called during initialization before lookups for consistent behavior.

functions.name: http_mimetype_find
functions.description: Finds the MIME type FIOBJ associated with a file extension. Returns a String on success or FIOBJ_INVALID on failure. Caller must fiobj_free the returned object.
requirements: file_ext must point to the extension bytes (without dot) of length file_ext_len.
Caller must check for FIOBJ_INVALID and must call fiobj_free on a successful return.

functions.name: http_mimetype_find2
functions.description: Returns the MIME type FIOBJ associated with a URL or the default HTTP MIME type. Caller must fiobj_free the returned object.
requirements: url must be a valid FIOBJ String-like object representing a URL/path.
Caller must call fiobj_free on the returned object.

functions.name: http_mimetype_clear
functions.description: Clears the internal MIME type registry, removing all associations.
requirements: Should typically be called during shutdown or before reinitializing MIME registry.

functions.name: http_req2str
functions.description: Returns a FIOBJ String representing the unparsed HTTP request (HTTP/1.1-capped), useful for proxying or debugging.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle for a request.
Caller must manage the returned FIOBJ per library ownership rules (likely requires fiobj_free when done).

functions.name: http_write_log
functions.description: Writes a log line to stderr describing the request/response. Invoked automatically when settings.log is enabled.
requirements: h must be a valid http_s handle.

functions.name: http_gmtime
functions.description: Converts a time_t to UTC (GMT) as struct tm, faster than gmtime_r for post-epoch times, falling back to gmtime_r for pre-epoch. Writes into tmbuf and returns it.
requirements: tmbuf must point to a valid writable struct tm.
timer is the input Unix time.

functions.name: http_date2rfc7231
functions.description: Formats the given struct tm as an RFC 7231 HTTP-date into target and returns the number of bytes written (~29–32).
requirements: target must point to a writable buffer with at least ~32 bytes available.
tmbuf must point to a valid UTC tm; use http_gmtime or equivalent.

functions.name: http_date2rfc2109
functions.description: Formats the given struct tm as an RFC 2109 cookie-date into target and returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: target must be a writable buffer sufficiently large (~32 bytes).
tmbuf must be a valid UTC tm.

functions.name: http_date2rfc2822
functions.description: Formats the given struct tm as an RFC 2822 date string into target and returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: target must be a writable buffer sufficiently large (~32 bytes).
tmbuf must be a valid UTC tm.

functions.name: http_time2str
functions.description: Formats a Unix time as an HTTP-date string into target. Uses cached results for faster processing at the cost of reduced precision. Returns number of bytes written.
requirements: target must point to a writable buffer with at least ~32 bytes available.
t is the input Unix time to format.

functions.name: http_decode_url_unsafe
functions.description: Decodes a URL-encoded string into dest without buffer overflow protection. Returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: dest must be a writable buffer large enough to hold the fully decoded result plus terminator if required.
url_data must be a NUL-terminated C string.
Caller is responsible for avoiding overflows (unsafe variant).

functions.name: http_decode_url
functions.signature: ssize_t http_decode_url(char *dest, const char *url_data, size_t length);
functions.description: Decodes a URL-encoded string (query/form data) into dest, reading at most length bytes from url_data. Returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: dest must be a writable buffer large enough for the decoded output.
url_data must reference at least length bytes of readable memory.
length specifies the input length; dest size is not checked—caller must ensure capacity.

functions.name: http_decode_path_unsafe
functions.description: Decodes the path component of a URL into dest without buffer overflow protection. Returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: dest must be a writable buffer large enough for the decoded path.
url_data must be a NUL-terminated C string.
Caller is responsible for avoiding overflows (unsafe variant).

functions.name: http_decode_path
functions.signature: ssize_t http_decode_path(char *dest, const char *url_data, size_t length);
functions.description: Decodes the path component of a URL into dest, processing at most length bytes. Returns the number of bytes written.
requirements: dest must be a writable buffer large enough for the decoded output.
url_data must reference at least length bytes of readable memory.
Caller must ensure dest capacity; function does not enforce bounds.

functions.name: http_tests
functions.description: Internal test routine available only in DEBUG builds. When compiled with DEBUG, runs HTTP-related tests.
requirements: Available only when DEBUG is defined at compile time.
Should be called in test contexts; not intended for production use.

functions.name: websocket_attach
functions.signature: void websocket_attach(intptr_t uuid, http_settings_s *http_settings, websocket_settings_s *args, void *data, size_t length);
functions.description: Attaches the WebSocket protocol to an existing socket/connection. Intended for internal use to transition an HTTP connection (or raw socket) into a WebSocket, applying the provided HTTP and WebSocket settings and any initial data buffer.
requirements: uuid must reference a valid, connected socket handled by the library (internal use).
http_settings must point to a valid http_settings_s structure configured for the connection.
args must point to a valid websocket_settings_s configuration structure.
If data is non-NULL, it must point to a readable buffer of size length; length must correctly represent the buffer size.
Callers should treat this as an internal/low-level API; behavior and stability are not guaranteed for external use.

functions.name: websocket_udata_get
functions.description: Returns the opaque user data pointer currently associated with the given WebSocket object. Useful for storing and retrieving per-connection state.
requirements: ws must be a valid pointer to an active or existing WebSocket object.

functions.name: websocket_udata_set
functions.description: Sets the opaque user data pointer on the given WebSocket object and returns the previous value (if any). Use to attach per-connection context.
requirements: ws must be a valid pointer to an active or existing WebSocket object.
udata may be any pointer value; lifecycle management of the pointed-to data is the caller's responsibility.

functions.name: websocket_uuid
functions.description: Returns the underlying socket UUID for the given WebSocket object. This is intended for locating the protocol object from outside WebSocket event callbacks; the socket itself should not be written to directly.
requirements: ws must be a valid pointer to a WebSocket object.
Callers must not write to the socket using the returned UUID; use the provided WebSocket APIs for I/O.

functions.name: websocket_is_client
functions.description: Returns 1 if the WebSocket connection operates in client mode (connected to a remote server) and 0 if it operates in server mode (accepted by the facil.io HTTP server).
requirements: ws must be a valid pointer to a WebSocket object.

functions.name: websocket_write
functions.signature: int websocket_write(ws_s *ws, fio_str_info_s msg, uint8_t is_text);
functions.description: Writes a message to the WebSocket. The is_text flag selects a text frame (non-zero) or a binary frame (zero). Returns 0 on success and -1 on failure.
requirements: ws must be a valid, open WebSocket connection.
msg must describe a valid, readable buffer for the duration of the call (data and length fields within fio_str_info_s must be consistent).
is_text must be 0 for binary frames or non-zero for text frames.

functions.name: websocket_close
functions.description: Closes the WebSocket connection. Triggers cleanup and revokes subscriptions associated with the socket.
requirements: ws must be a valid pointer to a WebSocket object; calling after it is already closed has unspecified behavior (not documented).

functions.name: websocket_subscribe
functions.description: Subscribes the provided WebSocket to a pub/sub channel or pattern as described by websocket_subscribe_s. Returns a non-zero subscription ID on success and 0 on failure. Subscriptions are automatically revoked when the WebSocket is closed. If the same channel is subscribed to multiple times, message delivery is merged but distinct subscription IDs are returned (each must be unsubscribed separately).
requirements: args.ws is REQUIRED and must be a valid, open WebSocket connection.
args.channel can be specified to subscribe to a specific channel; its fields must reference valid memory for the duration of the call.
If args.on_message is NULL, messages are forwarded directly to the client; optional force_binary/force_text may influence framing (force_binary has precedence).
If provided, args.on_unsubscribe must be callable for cleanup of args.udata.
If provided, args.match must be a valid pattern-matching callback.
Caller must handle a return value of 0 as failure and avoid using it with websocket_unsubscribe.

functions.name: websocket_unsubscribe
functions.description: Unsubscribes the given WebSocket from a previously created subscription identified by subscription_id. Failures are silent. Subscriptions are otherwise automatically revoked on WebSocket close; use this only while the WebSocket is open.
requirements: ws must be a valid, open WebSocket connection when this function is called.
subscription_id must be a valid ID previously returned by websocket_subscribe for the same WebSocket.
Should be called only while the WebSocket is open; after close, subscriptions are revoked automatically.

functions.name: websocket_optimize4broadcasts
functions.description: Enables or disables pub/sub broadcast optimizations for a connection or context. Optimizations can pre-wrap messages as WebSocket frames for direct transmission, reducing per-message overhead. Use types: WEBSOCKET_OPTIMIZE_PUBSUB, WEBSOCKET_OPTIMIZE_PUBSUB_TEXT, or WEBSOCKET_OPTIMIZE_PUBSUB_BINARY. Enabling/disabling is reference-counted per type; disable the same number of times it was enabled.
requirements: type should be one of WEBSOCKET_OPTIMIZE_PUBSUB, WEBSOCKET_OPTIMIZE_PUBSUB_TEXT, or WEBSOCKET_OPTIMIZE_PUBSUB_BINARY.
enable non-zero to enable, zero to disable; disables must be balanced with prior enables for the same type (reference-counted).
When enabled, pub/sub metadata may carry a pre-encoded WebSocket packet as an FIOBJ String; consumers should handle this optimized path if using message metadata externally.

functions.name: http1_new
functions.signature: fio_protocol_s *http1_new(uintptr_t uuid, http_settings_s *settings, void *unread_data, size_t unread_length);
functions.description: Creates and returns a new HTTP/1.x protocol object bound to the given connection/UUID and applies any unread bytes already received for that connection. Typical usage: call when upgrading/initializing a connection to HTTP/1.x, optionally providing a buffer of pending data that was read before the protocol object existed. Details about ownership and lifetime of the returned object are not stated in this header; treat the returned pointer as an opaque protocol instance managed by the facil.io runtime.
requirements: uuid must be a valid connection/descriptor identifier as used by the surrounding I/O framework (inferred from naming and common patterns).
settings must be a valid, initialized http_settings_s pointer for the lifetime required by the protocol (exact lifetime not specified; at minimum it must be valid during this call).
If unread_length > 0, unread_data must be non-NULL and point to at least unread_length bytes of readable memory containing pending HTTP/1.x data; if unread_length == 0, unread_data may be NULL.
Caller must check the returned pointer before use if the implementation may return NULL on failure (return behavior not documented here; this is unknown).

functions.name: http1_destroy
functions.description: Manually destroys an HTTP/1.x protocol object previously created by http1_new. Use when explicit teardown of the protocol is required rather than relying on automatic lifecycle management.
requirements: The argument must be a valid pointer to an HTTP/1.x protocol object created by http1_new.
Passing NULL or an invalid/non-HTTP1 protocol pointer results in undefined behavior (not documented; avoid).
Do not use the protocol object after calling this function (no further calls or dereferences).
Ensure the protocol is not concurrently in use by other threads/callbacks when destroying it (thread-safety not documented; avoid concurrent access).

functions.name: http1_vtable
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the HTTP/1.x protocol’s virtual function table (VTable). Intended for frameworks/components that need the protocol’s method table to register or interact with the protocol implementation.
requirements: Caller must treat the returned VTable pointer as opaque and not modify its contents.
The returned pointer must only be used in contexts expecting the HTTP/1.x protocol VTable for this library/version.
No arguments are required; may be called at initialization time to obtain the VTable.

functions.name: redis_engine_create
functions.description: Creates a Redis-backed pub/sub engine for facil.io. The engine connects to a Redis server (address/port/auth taken from redis_engine_create_args) and sends a periodic PING per ping_interval. The engine becomes active only once facil.io is running. Note: the engine assumes it will live until all queued messages and callbacks finish; destroying it prematurely may leak memory. A convenience macro allows designated-initializer call syntax.
requirements: facil.io must be running for the engine to become active (the engine is inactive until facil.io starts).
The engine object must remain alive until all outstanding messages and callbacks complete; destroying it earlier can cause memory leaks.
ping_interval is an 8-bit value; when 0, it falls back to facil.io’s default inactivity threshold (approximately 5 minutes).
If address/port/auth are omitted, defaults are used (address defaults to localhost; port defaults to 6379; auth default is unset).
Caller must supply a properly initialized struct redis_engine_create_args (fields are fio_str_info_s for address/port/auth; details of fio_str_info_s initialization are defined elsewhere).

functions.name: redis_engine_send
functions.signature: intptr_t redis_engine_send(fio_pubsub_engine_s *engine, FIOBJ command, void (*callback)(fio_pubsub_engine_s *e, FIOBJ reply, void *udata), void *udata);
functions.description: Sends a Redis command via the engine’s connection. Optionally provides a callback that receives the reply along with the user data. Commands are retried on network failures until a reply confirms delivery or the engine is destroyed. Do not use this for Redis Pub/Sub commands, as it will violate the connection’s protocol and can cause disconnections or message loss.
requirements: engine must be a valid pointer to a running redis engine created by redis_engine_create.
command must represent a valid Redis command in the library’s FIOBJ format (exact construction is library-specific and not documented here).
callback may be NULL; if provided, it must be callable in the engine’s callback context and tolerate asynchronous invocation.
udata is passed through unchanged to the callback and must remain valid for the duration of the command’s lifecycle.
Do NOT send Redis Pub/Sub commands (e.g., SUBSCRIBE/PSUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE) using this function, as it breaks the connection protocol.
Commands may be retried on network failures; callers must be prepared for the callback to run once upon successful validation or not at all if the engine is destroyed before validation.
The function returns an intptr_t identifier/status (exact semantics are unknown from this header).

functions.name: redis_engine_destroy
functions.description: Destroys the Redis engine and releases associated resources. Intended to be called when the engine is no longer needed. Note: destroying the engine while there are pending messages or callbacks can cause memory leaks, per the header’s caution.
requirements: engine must be a valid pointer to a redis engine (or NULL if allowed by implementation; behavior for NULL is not specified here).
Call only after ensuring all pending messages and callbacks have completed to avoid memory leaks.
Should be called when the engine is no longer needed; further use of engine after destruction is invalid.

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid, interesting arbitrary byte sequences (<=4096 bytes)
# tuned for the target stubs:
# - Hash inputs (siphash/risky_hash/fiobj_hash_string)
# - Base64 encode inputs
# - SHA1/SHA2 write buffers
# - JSON parsing inputs
# - HTTP-related decoders and headers (URL/path decode, cookie/header values)
# - FIO logging with %s (std::string safe)
# - fiobj_str_new raw bytes
# - WebSocket payloads and pub/sub messages
#
# Strategy: compose a small corpus of structured records and random blocks, then
# pick a scenario seeded by the given seed. Ensure buffers are NUL-safe (may include NULs),
# include both short and medium sizes, and sometimes include special characters
# useful for exercising decoders and parsers.

MAX_OUT = 4096

ASCII_CHARS = (
    [ord(c) for c in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789"] +
    [ord(c) for c in " -._~:/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;=%"]  # URL/HTTP-friendly set
)

CONTROL_BYTES = list(range(0x00, 0x20)) + [0x7f]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "こんにちは",  # Japanese
    "Привет",     # Russian
    "مرحبا",       # Arabic
    "😀😁😂🤣😜",   # Emojis
    "Γειά σου",   # Greek
    "हेलो",        # Hindi
]

JSON_SAMPLES = [
    b"{}",
    b"[]",
    b"\"string\"",
    b"12345",
    b"true",
    b"false",
    b"null",
    b"{\"a\":1,\"b\":[2,3],\"c\":\"x\"}",
    b"[{\"k\":\"v\"},{\"n\":0}]",
]

URL_SAMPLES = [
    b"/",
    b"/index.html",
    b"/a/b/c%2Fz?q=1&x=y",
    b"/spaces%20and%20more",
    b"/percent%25encoded",
]

BASE64_SAMPLES = [
    b"", b"f", b"fo", b"foo", b"foob", b"fooba", b"foobar",
]

WS_SAMPLES = [
    b"hello", b"binary\x00data", b"text with unicode: \xcf\x80",
]

HTTP_HEADER_SAMPLES = [
    b"Content-Type: text/plain",
    b"Set-Cookie: a=b; Path=/; HttpOnly",
    b"X-Custom: value-123",
]

# Helper builders

def _rand_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _ascii_bytes(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(r.choice(ASCII_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _control_heavy(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    pool = CONTROL_BYTES + [10, 13, 9]  # include LF, CR, TAB prominently
    return bytes(r.choice(pool) for _ in range(n))


def _utf8_blob(r: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    s = r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    # Repeat to increase size but keep under max_len
    rep = max(1, min(8, max_len // max(1, len(s))))
    data = (s * rep).encode('utf-8', 'strict')
    return data[:max_len]


def _concat_limit(chunks: List[bytes], limit: int) -> bytes:
    out = b""
    for c in chunks:
        if len(out) + len(c) > limit:
            out += c[: max(0, limit - len(out))]
            break
        out += c
    return out


def _make_scenario(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose a scenario family
    which = r.randrange(12)

    if which == 0:
        # JSON-centric buffer possibly followed by noise
        core = r.choice(JSON_SAMPLES)
        # Maybe append ASCII or controls to allow partial parsing
        suffix_kind = r.randrange(3)
        if suffix_kind == 0:
            suf = _ascii_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 128))
        elif suffix_kind == 1:
            suf = _control_heavy(r, r.randint(0, 64))
        else:
            suf = b""
        return _concat_limit([core, suf], MAX_OUT)

    if which == 1:
        # URL/path decoding focused payload
        core = r.choice(URL_SAMPLES)
        # Mix in additional percent-encodings and path separators
        extra = _ascii_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 256)).replace(b" ", b"%20")
        return _concat_limit([core, b"&p=%7Ehome", extra], MAX_OUT)

    if which == 2:
        # Base64 friendly chunk plus random tail
        core = r.choice(BASE64_SAMPLES)
        pad = _ascii_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 128))
        return _concat_limit([core, pad], MAX_OUT)

    if which == 3:
        # HTTP-like header lines joined by CRLF
        lines = r.sample(HTTP_HEADER_SAMPLES, k=r.randint(1, len(HTTP_HEADER_SAMPLES)))
        blob = b"\r\n".join(lines) + b"\r\n\r\n"
        add = _ascii_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 128))
        return _concat_limit([blob, add], MAX_OUT)

    if which == 4:
        # WebSocket application-level message candidates
        prefix = r.choice([b"", b"text:", b"bin:"])
        body_choice = r.choice(WS_SAMPLES)
        rand_tail = _rand_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 64))
        return _concat_limit([prefix, body_choice, rand_tail], MAX_OUT)

    if which == 5:
        # Mixed ASCII + NULs for binary-safe string creation and hashing
        a = _ascii_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 512))
        zeros = b"\x00" * r.randint(1, 64)
        b = _rand_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 256))
        return _concat_limit([a, zeros, b], MAX_OUT)

    if which == 6:
        # Control-heavy to exercise decoders and parsers
        ctrl = _control_heavy(r, r.randint(16, 512))
        mix = _ascii_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 256))
        return _concat_limit([ctrl, mix], MAX_OUT)

    if which == 7:
        # UTF-8 rich content for text paths (headers, json strings, ws text)
        u = _utf8_blob(r, r.randint(16, 1024))
        sep = b"\n" if r.randrange(2) else b"\r\n"
        return _concat_limit([u, sep, u[: r.randint(0, len(u))]], MAX_OUT)

    if which == 8:
        # Large random but bounded for hashing paths; keep <= 2048
        n = r.randint(1, 2048)
        return _rand_bytes(r, n)

    if which == 9:
        # Path with mixed encodings and reserved characters
        parts = [b"/api/v1/", _ascii_bytes(r, r.randint(1, 32))]
        parts.append(b"/%7Bid%7D?x=1&y=2%20z")
        parts.append(b"#frag")
        return _concat_limit(parts, MAX_OUT)

    if which == 10:
        # Cookie-like name=value;value with attributes
        name = _ascii_bytes(r, r.randint(1, 16)).replace(b";", b"_")
        value = _ascii_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 64))
        cookie = name + b"=" + value + b"; Path=/; HttpOnly; Max-Age=" + str(r.randint(0, 864000)).encode()
        return cookie[:MAX_OUT]

    # which == 11:
    # Combined structured then random tail to diversify slices
    head = r.choice([b"abc", b"{\"k\":\"v\"}", b"/x%2Fy", b"\r\n\r\n"])
    middle = _ascii_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 256))
    tail = _rand_bytes(r, r.randint(0, 512))
    return _concat_limit([head, middle, tail], MAX_OUT)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Produce 1..3 concatenated scenarios to broaden coverage while staying under limit
    count = 1 + (r.randrange(3))
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(count):
        chunks.append(_make_scenario(r))
    out = _concat_limit(chunks, MAX_OUT)

    # Ensure sometimes empty output (useful for len==0 with NULL data cases in stubs)
    if len(out) > 0 and (seed % 11 == 0):
        return b""

    return out

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path string
# Goal: produce valid, existing, writable file paths suitable for open(O_RDWR|O_CREAT)
# and for APIs that require an existing readable file. We'll create short, portable
# relative paths with simple names and optional subdirectories, ensuring the
# directories exist within the fuzzer's working directory namespace.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"

def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len=6, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))

def _maybe_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    exts = [".txt", ".bin", ".dat", ".cfg", ".pem", ".crt", ".key", ""]
    return rng.choice(exts)

def _ensure_dir(path: str) -> None:
    try:
        os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
    except Exception:
        pass

def _make_file(path: str, size: int, rng: random.Random) -> None:
    # Create file with random content of given size; overwrite if exists.
    # Ensure parent dirs exist.
    parent = os.path.dirname(path)
    if parent:
        _ensure_dir(parent)
    try:
        with open(path, 'wb') as f:
            # write deterministic but varied content
            chunk = bytearray(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(min(4096, size)))
            total = 0
            while total < size:
                to_write = min(size - total, len(chunk))
                f.write(chunk[:to_write])
                total += to_write
    except Exception:
        # Best effort: if write fails, attempt to create empty file
        try:
            with open(path, 'wb'):
                pass
        except Exception:
            pass

def _candidate_paths(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Build a small set of interesting path shapes under a prefix directory.
    base = os.path.abspath(os.getcwd())
    prefix_choices = [
        os.path.join(base, "fuzz-tmp"),
        os.path.join(base, "fuzz-tmp", "a"),
        os.path.join(base, "fuzz-tmp", "b", "c"),
        os.path.join(base, "fuzz-tmp", "unix"),
    ]
    for d in prefix_choices:
        _ensure_dir(d)
    paths = []
    # Simple flat files
    for _ in range(3):
        paths.append(os.path.join(prefix_choices[0], _rand_name(rng) + _maybe_ext(rng)))
    # Nested directories
    for _ in range(3):
        paths.append(os.path.join(prefix_choices[1], _rand_name(rng) + _maybe_ext(rng)))
    for _ in range(3):
        paths.append(os.path.join(prefix_choices[2], _rand_name(rng) + _maybe_ext(rng)))
    # Files with dots and dashes
    for _ in range(3):
        name = _rand_name(rng, 3, 8) + "-" + _rand_name(rng, 3, 8) + _maybe_ext(rng)
        paths.append(os.path.join(prefix_choices[0], name))
    # Hidden-like names
    for _ in range(2):
        name = "." + _rand_name(rng, 3, 8) + _maybe_ext(rng)
        paths.append(os.path.join(prefix_choices[0], name))
    return paths

def _prepare_files(paths: List[str], rng: random.Random) -> None:
    # Create content sized to exercise various APIs: small, medium slices
    for p in paths:
        sz = rng.choice([0, 1, 13, 64, 257, 1024, 2048])
        _make_file(p, sz, rng)

def _choose_existing_path(rng: random.Random, paths: List[str]) -> str:
    # Prefer an existing file; fall back to a random new path under fuzz-tmp
    existing = [p for p in paths if os.path.isfile(p)]
    if existing:
        return rng.choice(existing)
    # Fallback: create one now
    p = os.path.join(os.path.abspath(os.getcwd()), "fuzz-tmp", _rand_name(rng) + _maybe_ext(rng))
    _make_file(p, rng.choice([0, 64, 1024]), rng)
    return p

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Prepare a pool of files
    paths = _candidate_paths(rng)
    _prepare_files(paths, rng)

    # Decide which target usage to favor based on seed buckets
    mode = seed % 6
    if mode == 0:
        # Generic readable/writable file for open(O_RDWR|O_CREAT)
        chosen = _choose_existing_path(rng, paths)
    elif mode == 1:
        # Likely certificate/key-like names for TLS APIs
        dirp = os.path.join(os.path.abspath(os.getcwd()), "fuzz-tmp", "certs")
        _ensure_dir(dirp)
        names = ["server", "client", "root", _rand_name(rng)]
        suffix = rng.choice([".crt", ".pem", ".key"]) 
        chosen = os.path.join(dirp, rng.choice(names) + suffix)
        _make_file(chosen, rng.choice([256, 1024, 2048]), rng)
    elif mode == 2:
        # Path with URL-encoded-looking segments for http_sendfile2 decode join
        dirp = os.path.join(os.path.abspath(os.getcwd()), "fuzz-tmp", "paths")
        _ensure_dir(dirp)
        raw = _rand_name(rng, 4, 10) + _maybe_ext(rng)
        chosen = os.path.join(dirp, raw)
        _make_file(chosen, rng.choice([13, 64, 257]), rng)
    elif mode == 3:
        # Deeper nested
        dirp = os.path.join(os.path.abspath(os.getcwd()), "fuzz-tmp", _rand_name(rng,3,6), _rand_name(rng,3,6))
        _ensure_dir(dirp)
        chosen = os.path.join(dirp, _rand_name(rng) + _maybe_ext(rng))
        _make_file(chosen, rng.choice([0, 64, 1024]), rng)
    elif mode == 4:
        # Hidden file
        dirp = os.path.join(os.path.abspath(os.getcwd()), "fuzz-tmp")
        _ensure_dir(dirp)
        chosen = os.path.join(dirp, "." + _rand_name(rng) + _maybe_ext(rng))
        _make_file(chosen, rng.choice([1, 64, 2048]), rng)
    else:
        # Short relative name in base fuzz-tmp
        dirp = os.path.join(os.path.abspath(os.getcwd()), "fuzz-tmp")
        _ensure_dir(dirp)
        chosen = os.path.join(dirp, _rand_name(rng, 3, 8) + _maybe_ext(rng))
        _make_file(chosen, rng.choice([0, 64, 1024]), rng)

    # Return bytes of the path string (C-string style, without null terminator)
    data = chosen.encode('utf-8')
    # Ensure size <= 4096
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
